sources.title: Batch 0058 frozen repository source context for InnoDB versus MyISAM
Frozen MySQL 8.4 primary-source research for InnoDB versus MyISAM

claims.text: All four frozen Question IDs compare InnoDB and MyISAM; one variant additionally asks what MySQL storage engines exist, which the candidate answers through version-bound examples plus SHOW ENGINES discovery.
MySQL 8.4 uses InnoDB as the default/general-purpose engine; InnoDB supports transactions and crash recovery while MyISAM does not support transactions.

The candidate preserves InnoDB row-level locking/consistent-read semantics versus MyISAM table-level locking without claiming InnoDB locks exactly one row or that MyISAM has zero conditional write concurrency.
The candidate covers the supported MySQL 8.4 differences in MVCC, foreign keys and clustered-index organization while keeping deeper B+Tree details outside the comparison scope.

The candidate binds claims to MySQL 8.4, avoids the obsolete MyISAM-only FULLTEXT claim, treats supported-engine discovery as runtime-specific and rejects universal speed rankings in favor of workload/semantic selection.
